title: Types of metamorphosis
keyIdea: Metamorphosis is the big change in body shape as some animals grow up. Insects grow it in two ways. In complete metamorphosis there are 4 stages: egg, larva, pupa, adult. The larva, like a caterpillar, looks nothing like the adult, and inside the pupa its body is rebuilt with wings. Butterflies, beetles, flies and bees grow this way. In incomplete metamorphosis there are 3 stages: egg, nymph, adult, with no pupa. The nymph looks like a small adult without full wings and moults its hard skin to grow. Grasshoppers, crickets and dragonflies grow this way.
familyTip: Look under leaves and in a pond net with your child. If you find a young insect, ask: does it look like a small adult (a nymph) or nothing like it (a larva)? Shed grasshopper or dragonfly skins are sometimes left on stems; they show the insect climbed out to grow.

visual.caption: Complete or incomplete metamorphosis? Drag each insect, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: moult a growing grasshopper, build two life cycles, sort insects by their young, look inside a chrysalis, and feed young and adult insects.

kid: An insect has a hard skin on the outside. It cannot stretch. So a young insect grows in steps. It splits its old skin and climbs out with a new, bigger one. This is called moulting.

Some insects change shape completely as they grow. A butterfly starts as an egg. Out comes a larva, the caterpillar. It eats and grows. Then it makes a pupa, the chrysalis. Inside, its body is taken apart and built again, with wings. Then out comes the adult. That is 4 stages.

Other insects change a little at a time. A grasshopper starts as an egg. Out comes a nymph. It looks like a small grasshopper with no wings. Each time it moults, it gets bigger and its wings grow. That is 3 stages, and there is no pupa.
A caterpillar chews leaves, but a butterfly sips nectar. So the young and the adult do not fight over food. A young grasshopper eats grass, just like the adult.
adult: Ages 9 to 11. This fits the National Curriculum in England for Year 5: describe the differences in the life cycles of a mammal, an amphibian, an insect and a bird. Complete metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult) is found in butterflies and moths, beetles, flies, bees, wasps and ants. Incomplete or gradual metamorphosis (egg, nymph, adult) is found in grasshoppers, crickets, cockroaches, dragonflies and true bugs.

An insect's exoskeleton stretches only a little, so it is shed in a moult. A monarch caterpillar has five larval stages called instars. Grasshopper nymphs moult five or six times, and their wing pads grow at each moult until the last moult gives working wings. Adult insects do not moult or grow any more. Inside a monarch chrysalis, which lasts about 10 to 14 days, many larval tissues are broken down while groups of cells called imaginal discs grow into wings, legs, eyes and a sipping proboscis. Larva and adult usually eat different food, so they do not compete.

Common mistakes: thinking the hard skin stretches; that every insect has a pupa; that a pupa is asleep and doing nothing; that a small butterfly is a baby that will grow; and that spiders are insects. Spiders have 8 legs, and their young simply moult. Note that a dragonfly nymph lives under water and looks fairly different from the adult, but it still has no pupa.

In the lab your child feeds a grasshopper nymph and helps it out of its old skin five times, builds a butterfly and a grasshopper life cycle, sorts seven animals using clues about their young, drags through ten days inside a chrysalis, and matches foods to a caterpillar, a butterfly, a nymph and an adult grasshopper.

practice.prompt: In metamorphosis, which life cycle has a pupa stage?
practice.hint: Complete metamorphosis has 4 stages. Which stage is missing from egg, nymph, adult?
practice.explain: Only complete metamorphosis has a pupa: egg, larva, pupa, adult. Incomplete is egg, nymph, adult.

practice.prompt: A grasshopper nymph has moulted {n} times. It needs {k} moults in all to become an adult. How many more moults are left?
practice.hint: Take the moults it has done away from the moults it needs in all.
practice.explain: {k} − {n} = {=k-n} more moults. Each one gives it a bigger skin and bigger wing buds.

practice.prompt: A young insect looks like a small adult with no full wings. What is it called?
practice.hint: A larva looks nothing like the adult. A pupa does not walk about.
practice.explain: It is a nymph. Nymphs look like small adults and grow wings bit by bit as they moult.

practice.prompt: A butterfly egg hatches after {n} days. The caterpillar eats for {k} days, and the chrysalis lasts 10 days. How many days is that from egg to adult?
practice.hint: Add the three parts: days as an egg, days as a caterpillar, and 10 days as a chrysalis.
practice.explain: {n} + {k} + 10 = {=n+k+10} days from egg to adult butterfly.

pool.prompt: Why must a young grasshopper moult?
choices: Its hard skin cannot stretch, so it needs a new, bigger one
pool.hint: Think about the hard skin on the outside. Can it get bigger?
pool.explain: An insect's hard outer skin cannot stretch much, so it splits it and grows a bigger one.

pool.prompt: Which insect grows by complete metamorphosis?
pool.hint: Which one has a young larva that later makes a pupa?
pool.explain: A ladybird has a spiky larva and then a pupa, so it has all 4 stages.

choices: The body is taken apart and rebuilt with wings
pool.hint: What has the butterfly got that the caterpillar did not have?
pool.explain: Inside, much of the caterpillar's body breaks down and groups of cells build wings, legs and eyes.

pool.prompt: A small butterfly and a big butterfly are the same kind. Is the small one a baby?
choices: No: adult butterflies do not grow
pool.hint: Do adult insects still moult? Without a moult, can an insect get bigger?
pool.explain: No. Adult insects do not moult, so they do not grow. A small one is just a small adult.

pool.prompt: Why does a spider not fit either type of insect metamorphosis?
choices: A spider is not an insect
pool.explain: A spider has 8 legs, so it is not an insect. Its young look like tiny spiders and just moult.

pool.prompt: A caterpillar and a butterfly do not fight over food. Why?
choices: The caterpillar chews leaves; the butterfly sips nectar
pool.hint: Think about their mouths: jaws or a long tube?
pool.explain: The caterpillar chews leaves and the butterfly sips nectar, so they eat different food.

pool.prompt: Complete metamorphosis has 4 stages and incomplete has 3. A scientist draws the life cycles of {n} butterflies and {k} grasshoppers. How many stages does she draw in all?
pool.hint: Each butterfly has 4 stages and each grasshopper has 3. Work out both, then add.

pool.prompt: What is the order of stages in complete metamorphosis?
pool.hint: The larva hatches from the egg, then it makes a pupa.
pool.explain: Egg, larva, pupa, adult: the larva eats and grows, then rebuilds inside the pupa.

pool.prompt: A grasshopper nymph moults about every {n} days, and it moults 5 times. About how many days is it a nymph?
pool.hint: It moults 5 times, with about {n} days between moults. Work out 5 lots of {n}.
pool.explain: 5 × {n} = {=5*n} days as a nymph. After the 5th moult it is an adult with full wings.
